subject: Re: Horizon Data — KMS/TLS proof package & delivery schedule
messages:
From: security@horizondata.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@horizondata.com, erika.leung@sigma-audits.com
Date: Sun, 1 Mar 2026 08:17:00 -0700
Subject: KMS/TLS artifacts for SIG/CAIQ review

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the walkthrough earlier. Horizon’s security team is finalizing the SIG/CAIQ responses and our auditor (Erika from Sigma) needs two short proof sets to close controls related to encryption:  

1) KMS/HSM: signed attestation that Redwood uses an HSM-backed KMS for tenant key wrapping, plus a sample of a recent rotation audit (redacted to remove tenant IDs). We don’t need full logs — a 10-line CSV with timestamp, key_id (hashed), actor_role, and rotation_action should suffice.  

2) In-transit: a short TLS cipher-suite report for the public API endpoints (last 30 days) showing accepted protocols/ciphers and the most recent cert fingerprint.

Can you confirm what artifacts you can provide by EOD Thursday (3/5)? Also advise whether these can be delivered to our secure intake link (https://horizon-secure.intake/s3) or if you prefer Redwood Drive.

Erika — copying you so you can chime on sufficiency.

Appreciate the quick turn.

—Alex
Head of Security, Horizon Data

--
Attachment: none
From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: security@horizondata.com
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, erika.leung@sigma-audits.com
Date: Mon, 2 Mar 2026 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: KMS/TLS artifacts for SIG/CAIQ review

Alex — thanks, we can do that. Looping in Jonas for the cryptography artifacts and Laura for any legal/redaction guidance on logs. Ben is copied to coordinate delivery and timing relative to the deal timeline.

Quick answers up front:  
- We can provide a signed HSM attestation (PDF) signed by our HSM vendor plus a redacted rotation log sample (CSV) that matches the columns you requested.
- TLS cipher-suite summary for the last 30 days and the current cert fingerprint — we’ll include a short explanation of our TLS termination topology (edge LB -> internal proxies -> runtime) to make the control narrative clear.
- Preferred delivery: Redwood secure Drive share (link will be time-limited) unless Horizon needs it pushed to your intake bucket; we can also SFTP if that’s required.

Jonas — can you produce the rotation sample and an example of the access matrix row (redacted) we typically ship to auditors? Please note we must redact tenant IDs and exact actor emails; we can map to roles (e.g., ops:rotation-service, infra:rotation-operator, support:escalation-pager).

Laura — any constraints on sending a vendor-signed attestation (pdf) to an external intake URL?

Goal: ship the bundle (attestation + rotation-snip + tls-report + access-matrix) by EOD Thu 3/5. If any of you foresee a blocker, flag it today.

Best,
Marissa
Director, Customer Security Operations
Redwood Inference

--
Attachment: request-summary.txt
From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, security@horizondata.com
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, erika.leung@sigma-audits.com
Date: Wed, 4 Mar 2026 09:21:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: KMS/TLS artifacts for SIG/CAIQ review

Alex / team — I pulled together the artifacts you’ll need. Plan below and included sample snippets in the secure share.

What we will provide:  
- hsm-attestation-signed.pdf: Vendor attestation confirming HSM-backed root for wrapping keys. Contains vendor signature, attestation scope, and a validity period.
- rotation-log-snip.csv: 10 lines, columns = [timestamp_iso, key_id_hash, actor_role, rotation_action, rotation_version]. All tenant-identifiers hashed and salts applied; we include a short note on the hash method.
- redacted-kms-access-matrix.csv: single-page export mapping roles -> permissions (redacted user emails replaced with role names).
- tls-cipher-report.txt: summary of accepted TLS versions/ciphers for api.redwood.ai for 2026-02-01 -> 2026-03-01 and SHA256 fingerprint for the current cert.

Delivery & provenance:  
- Files are packaged into a time-limited Redwood Drive folder. Link above is for download; we can also push to Horizon’s intake S3 if you provide a short-lived presigned URL (preferred for ingestion into your audit system).
- For audit provenance, we’ll include a small manifest (manifest.txt) listing the commands / APIs used to extract each artifact (e.g., cloud-kms audit-logs API call, internal rotation service query) and a PGP-signed checksum file so Sigma can validate integrity.

Notes on content sensitivity & redaction:  
- Rotation logs: we will redact tenant_id and direct user identifiers, but will not alter timestamps, key identifiers (they are hashed), nor rotation_action values. This preserves timeline integrity while keeping tenant data private.
- Access matrix includes role names only; we’ll provide a mapping file describing role responsibilities.

If this matches expectations I’ll finalize artifacts and upload by EOD Thu (3/5). Erika — if you need the raw audit export for deeper forensics, let us know; that requires a formal NDA addendum and I’ll route to Legal.

-Jonas
Senior Cryptography Engineer
Redwood Inference

--

Marissa / Jonas — this is exactly what we need, thanks. Two quick items before you upload: 

1) Horizon intake: please upload to our intake S3 using this short-lived presigned URL (sent separately by procurement). If that’s a problem, the Redwood Drive link is fine but we prefer S3.

2) For compliance, Sigma asked for a one-paragraph attestation from Redwood stating that the rotation sample is representative (i.e., not a synthetic or hand-crafted extract) and that the hash method used for key_id is disclosed. A signed one-paragraph note from you (or Jonas) will close the control.

Ben — procurement will want to align on timing for the next milestone payment tied to artifact delivery. Procurement — can you confirm receipt of the presigned URL?

We appreciate the quick turnaround — please proceed once the presigned link is visible.

—Alex
Head of Security, Horizon Data
